relations: Tonearm lowering at the pivot causes headshell and cartridge to drift slowly downward together.
Stylus vertical gap remains above the record edge throughout, never crossing onto the vinyl surface.
Record resting on the platter keeps its rim position fixed, showing no in-plane translation.
Shallow depth of field holds the blurred chassis and pivot in a pink haze during motion.
caption: The video captures an extreme close-up of a turntable rendered with a very shallow depth of field. A black vinyl record rests on a brushed-metal platter that fills the lower-left area, its rim catching a soft highlight. To the right, a tonearm terminates in a silver headshell secured by two small screws, holding a black cartridge and stylus assembly that hovers above the deck. The thin arm tube extends off the right border, and the blurred chassis and pivot area recede into a warm, pinkish haze. The headshell and cartridge undergo a small, slow downward drift, lowering slightly as the tonearm moves. The stylus remains clear of the record's edge for the entire duration, never crossing over the vinyl surface. The record itself shows no in-plane translation, its rim holding position relative to the platter. Only the gentle repositioning of the tonearm marks the visible change.
